title: "Roadmap"

## Project timeline

Delivered scope from inception to the v0.1 release, with the tracking issue
for each step. Every item below was completed as a tested pull request and
verified by execution; the dates are the issue-close dates.

**3 October — baseline**

- The product specification ([PRD](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/PRD.md)) is written and reviewed before implementation; the repository, CI, governance documents and website follow ([#1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/1), [#37](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/37)-[#56](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/56)).

**8 October — first capabilities**

- The rule engine runs a security rule against a test request and returns a verdict — the core decision loop, verified by fixtures ([#2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/2), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/59)).
- The kernel packet filter compiles, loads under the verifier and detaches cleanly — the eBPF environment is proven ([#3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/3), gate output in [lab](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/README.md)).

**9 October — packet path verified end to end**

- The kernel-to-engine event channel passes its end-to-end test in the lab: packets become structured events with correct field layout ([#4](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/4), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/81)).
- Requests are now scored stage-by-stage (the inspection ladder), with verdicts recorded at each stage ([#5](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/5)).
- HTTP request bodies are parsed into the structured view the rules operate on ([#5](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/5), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/88)).

**10 October — v0.1**

- The deployment lab is reproducible on demand: cluster, gateway, firewall and a demo application, with each network hop verified by response headers ([#6](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/6), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/96)).
- The firewall's verdicts match the vendor-neutral reference rule set (OWASP CRS) on every corpus case — 19/19, one documented gap — and the comparison is enforced in CI on all future changes ([#7](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/7), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/103)).
- A security policy written as a Kubernetes resource is compiled and loaded by the platform, and matching traffic is blocked; the apply-to-effect round trip is measured at 1.5–2.6 s against a 5 s budget ([#8](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/8), PRs [#98](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/98)/[#104](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/104)).
- Repeat offenders are dropped in the kernel, bans expire automatically, and every ban produces an evidence record ([#10](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/10), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/105)).
- Every verdict emits three correlated records — trace, metric, log — tied by request id ([#11](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/11), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/101)).
- Automated clients are distinguishable from browsers from traffic fingerprints, validated against published test vectors ([#12](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/12), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/99)).
- A route's published API schema acts as an allow-list: non-conforming requests are rejected with a diagnostic naming the violated field ([#13](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/13), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/102)).
- The platform's limits are stated rather than implied: the README exit checklist marks each acceptance criterion pass or pending with evidence links ([#14](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/14), [PR](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/pull/108)); the release is signed and published ([v0.1.0](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/releases/tag/v0.1.0)).

Every issue lands a runnable artefact with an exit criterion — prove the ladder end-to-end, not slide-by-slide.

## Sprint sequencing

The v0.1 sprint sequence: shield PoC → ingest → ladder slice → NGF steering lab → CRS differential → operator/CRD round-trip → ScoredWindowBan → OTel pipeline → bot v0 → positive security v0 → honest exit ([TR-14](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/14)).

## Contributing

Contributions follow the [contributing guide](contributing.html): pick an issue labeled `complexity:starter` or any `area:*` that suits you; the referenced PRD section in the issue body is the design source. Branch + PR against `trishula-dev/trishula` (MIT).
